page: Microsoft Azure HX176rs is an HX-family virtual machine configured with 176 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel processor using the x86_64 architecture. Managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server is designed for high-resource workloads, featuring 1408.0 GB of system memory, which equates to a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include any graphics processing units.

For storage, the instance is equipped with 4332 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity and is designated as Premium Storage capable. Additionally, the server features RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) capabilities, which support low-latency, high-throughput networking interfaces. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this configuration.

Given its high memory capacity, dedicated Intel vCPUs, and fast local NVMe SSD storage, this server is suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database hosting, and high-performance computing workloads that benefit from RDMA networking. The hardware profile offers high resource density, balancing massive memory allocation with substantial local storage capacity.
